name: assign_frame_load
title: Assign a frame load
description: Assigns a uniformly distributed load (kN/m over the whole length) or a point load (kN at a relative position 0–1) to frame objects under a load pattern. direction 10 = gravity by default (a positive value acts downward); 1–3 are the frame's local axes, 4–6 global X/Y/Z, 7–9 projected. Writes the model: the bridge saves it and copies a .EDB snapshot first; ETABS has no undo. [Registry tool v1, Load, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

loadType.description: Uniform distributed load or a single point load

valueKNperM.description: Distributed load in kN/m (positive = along the direction; downward for gravity directions 10/11)

relativePosition.description: Point load position as a fraction of the length from the I end

direction.description: 1–3 frame local axes, 4–6 global X/Y/Z, 7–9 projected global, 10 gravity, 11 projected gravity

replace.description: Replace existing loads of this pattern on the frame (false = add)

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: assign_frame_section
title: Assign a frame section
description: Assigns one frame section property to the given frame objects (unique names). Writes the model: the bridge saves it and copies a .EDB snapshot first; ETABS has no undo. Frames ETABS refuses are listed in errors. [Registry tool v1, Property, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: cancel_execution
title: Cancel running script
description: Signals cancellation to the script currently running in the host application. Cancellation is cooperative: the script stops at its next `ct` check, and its transaction group is rolled back. Returns whether anything was running.

name: draw_frame_by_coords
title: Draw a frame by coordinates
description: Adds one frame object between two points given in mm (global coordinates), optionally with a frame section and a user name. Writes the model: the bridge saves it and copies a .EDB snapshot first (see the result's snapshot); ETABS has no undo. Returns the new frame's unique name. [Registry tool v1, Geometry, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

section.description: Frame section property name; default the model's default section

name.description: User name for the new frame; default ETABS numbers it

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: execute_etabs_code
title: Execute C# in ETABS
description: Runs a C# script against the ETABS 22 model the HPEtabs MCP Bridge app is attached to (ETABSv1 API). Globals: sapModel (cSapModel), etabs (cOAPI), units (forced to kN_mm_C for the run: mm, kN, kN·mm, kN/mm²; restored after), ct, log(string), progress(cur,total,msg), args (args.Str/Int/Double/Bool(key, fallback)). OAPI calls return int: check ret, throw InvalidOperationException($"ETABS returned {ret} from X"); bad inputs → ArgumentException. End with `return <value>;`. No transaction or undo. Tiers, decided statically from `sapModel.X.Member(...)` chains (an alias, cast, ?., lambda or argument of a global = D): R read-only (Get*/Is*/Has*/Count/RefreshView/all of sapModel.Results/GetTableForDisplayArray; transaction=none). W write (other members; transaction=auto): the bridge saves your model and copies a .EDB snapshot first (`snapshot` names it); unsaved or UNC models are refused; rolledBack:false after an exception means the changes persisted. D destructive (SetModelIsLocked, RunAnalysis, DeleteResults, OpenFile/New*/Save, ApplyEditedTables, Start*/Modify*/Merge*/Reset*/Clear*/Rename*/Show*/Export*/Import*/Delete*, any path-taking member): needs 'Allow destructive operations' in the bridge window, else error -32001; up to 600 s. dryRun or transaction=none on a writing script = static preview (nothing runs; PREVIEW lists the members); manual = auto; changed counts additions/deletions only. cancel/timeout cannot interrupt a running ETABS call; the save counts against the timeout. Paths: a literal or args.Str("key") under the model folder or %LocalAppData%\HPEtabs, never UNC; every path-shaped args string is screened. No Helper/ApplicationExit/dialogs/#r/#load. Needs 'Allow AI code execution' in the HPEtabs MCP Bridge window (a separate app, not inside ETABS).

code.description: C# script body, max 32 KB. No `await`, no System.IO / System.Net / reflection / expression trees / interop, no Helper or application lifecycle calls, no dialogs (blocked by the guard).

transaction.description: auto (default): writing script — the bridge saves the model and takes a .EDB snapshot before running. none: read-only; a script that writes is refused with a PREVIEW diagnostic. manual: accepted for compatibility, behaves like auto.

dryRun.description: Static preview for a writing script (nothing runs; the PREVIEW diagnostic lists what it would call); a read-only script runs normally. Refused for destructive members.

timeoutSeconds.description: Cooperative timeout in seconds, 5–120 (up to 600 while destructive operations are allowed). Checked between OAPI calls only — a running RunAnalysis/Save/OpenFile cannot be interrupted.

label.description: Short name for the audit log and the snapshot file name. Max 64 characters; letters, digits, _ and - survive, the rest becomes _.

args.description: Optional JSON object handed to the script as `args` (e.g. {"frame": "12", "section": "C40x40"}). Keys are matched case-insensitively.

name: get_etabs_context
title: Get ETABS context
description: Returns the ETABS session the bridge app is attached to: hostVersion (22), docTitle and docPath of the model file (absent while no model is open or it was never saved), isModifiable (attached, a model is open, ETABS is idle — no dialog open), units.length (mm: every run forces kN_mm_C), executionEnabled, and etabs {isAttached, attachedPid, oapiVersion, isLocked (definitions cannot change until unlocked — unlocking discards results), presentUnits (the user's own API units), databaseUnits, destructiveOperationsEnabled (the second opt-in: unlock, RunAnalysis, file operations), pointCount, frameCount, areaCount}. With includeSelection the selected objects come back (max 50) as {id, category = object type, name}. Fails fast with a busy error while a script is running, with 'not attached' until the user clicks Attach in the HPEtabs MCP Bridge window, and with 'no model' on the ETABS start screen. Call this before execute_etabs_code so the script matches the real model and its lock state.

includeSelection.description: Include the objects currently selected in ETABS (max 50: id = running index, category = object type (Point/Frame/Area/…), name = object unique name).

name: get_frame_forces
title: Get frame forces
description: Internal forces along frame objects for one load case or combination: axial P, shears V2/V3 in kN, torsion T and moments M2/M3 in kN·m at each output station (mm from the I end). Needs analysis results (run_analysis first). Filter by frame names. Read-only. [Registry tool v1, Results, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

caseOrCombo.description: Load case or combination name whose results to read

frameNames.description: Only these frames — unique names from get_structural_objects.name, not labels; default every frame

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1–500)

name: get_joint_reactions
title: Get joint reactions
description: Reactions at the restrained joints for one load case or combination: forces in kN and moments in kN·m, per joint and step. Needs analysis results (run_analysis first, or run it in ETABS). Filter by point names or by story. Read-only — selecting the output case is a results setting, not a model change. [Registry tool v1, Results, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

caseOrCombo.description: Load case or combination name whose results to read

pointNames.description: Only these joints — unique names from get_structural_objects.name, not labels; default every joint with a reaction

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1–500)

name: get_load_definitions
title: Get load definitions
description: Lists the load patterns (type, self-weight multiplier), the load cases (type, sub-type) and the load combinations (type and, on request, the cases with their scale factors). Read-only. [Registry tool v1, Load, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

includeComboCases.description: Also list each combination's cases and scale factors

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1–500)

name: get_materials_and_sections
title: Get materials and frame sections
description: Lists the material properties (type, E in MPa, Poisson ratio, thermal coefficient, G in MPa) and the frame section properties (shape type, area in mm², I22/I33 in mm⁴, S/Z in mm³, radii of gyration in mm) defined in the model. Read-only. [Registry tool v1, Property, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1–500)

name: get_modal_results
title: Get modal results
description: Periods, frequencies and participating mass ratios (UX, UY, UZ, RX, RY, RZ with their sums) of the modal load case. Needs analysis results with a modal case (run_analysis first). Read-only. [Registry tool v1, Results, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1–500)

name: get_model_info
title: Get model info
description: Overview of the ETABS model the bridge is attached to: file name and folder, lock state, present and database units, ETABS version, object counts (points, frames, areas) and optionally the stories. Call it first: every script works in kN and mm whatever the model's units. Read-only. [Registry tool v1, Model, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

includeStories.description: Also list the stories with elevation and height in mm

name: get_run
title: Get a past run
description: Details of one run from the history (runId comes back from the execute tool, run_tool and test_tool): outcome, args, the code when it was a successful ad-hoc script, and — when the host application is reachable — an analysis listing hard-coded literals (line, value, variable) and the args keys already read. Use it before propose_tool to decide which literals become parameters.

analyze.description: Analyse the code (guard, compile, literals) through the host application

name: get_stories_and_grids
title: Get stories and grid systems
description: Lists the stories (name, elevation and height in mm, master/similar flags, splice) from the base up and the names of the grid systems. Read-only. [Registry tool v1, Geometry, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1–500)

name: get_structural_objects
title: Get structural objects
description: Pages through the frame, area or point objects: unique name, label and story, the frame section (areas: none — the API's section member is blocked), end points or vertices in mm and the frame length in mm. Filter by story or by a substring of the name. Read-only. [Registry tool v1, Geometry, transaction=none. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

story.description: Only objects on this story (exact story name)

nameLike.description: Only objects whose unique name or label contains this text (case-insensitive)

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (1–500)

name: get_tool
title: Get a registry tool
description: Full record of one stored tool: metadata, input schema, examples, C# code (optional), run statistics and recent runs.

recentRuns.description: How many recent runs to include (0–50)

name: inspect_type
title: Inspect a host API type
description: Reflects over an API type loaded in the running host application (Revit or AutoCAD) and returns its public members as C#-like signatures (kind: property | method | field | event). Use it to confirm exact method names and parameters before writing a script.

typeName.description: Type name, e.g. 'Wall' or 'FilteredElementCollector' in Revit, 'Polyline' or 'LayerTableRecord' in AutoCAD, or a fully qualified name such as 'Autodesk.Revit.DB.Structure.Rebar'.

memberFilter.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to keep only matching member names, e.g. 'Create'.

maxMembers.description: Maximum number of members to return (default 100, max 500).

name: manage_tool
title: Deprecate, quarantine or restore a tool
description: deprecate: retire a tool (never runs again until restored). quarantine: pull it from tools/list. restore: back to draft so it can be tested and published again.

annotations.title: Deprecate, quarantine or restore a tool

name: propose_tool
title: Propose a new registry tool
description: Package a working C# script as a reusable tool (status draft). Replace every literal that may change between calls with args.<Kind>("key") and declare each key in inputSchema (JSON Schema object: string/number/integer/boolean/array/object, required, default, description). The code is guard-checked and compiled inside the host application but not run. Give ≥ 2 examples with different args; test_tool runs them. Returns a validation report; fix errors and call again. Use newVersion=true to replace the code of an existing tool.

description.description: What the tool does, for search and for the reviewer (≥ 20 chars)

category.description: One of the host's categories (search_tools lists them): Architecture | Structure | MEP | Annotation | View | Data | Generic for Revit, Drawing | Layer | Block | Annotation | Layout | Data | Generic for AutoCAD

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the args object

code.description: Script body: same globals as the execute tool plus args; must end with return

title.description: Human title, e.g. 'Colour beams by type'

transaction.description: auto (the bridge wraps the run in a transaction) | manual (Revit: the code opens its own Transaction; AutoCAD: same as auto) | none (read-only)

sourceRunId.description: runId of the execute run this comes from (see get_run)

newVersion.description: Propose a new version of an existing tool name

name: publish_tool
title: Publish a registry tool
description: Request publication of a tested tool. Policy manual (default): the tool becomes pending_approval, a review file is written and a human must run the server's `registry approve <name>` command (`<server>.exe registry --help`; or set status=published in tool.json). Policy auto: tested tools publish immediately. Published tools appear in tools/list of every running server.

name: run_analysis
title: Run the analysis
description: DESTRUCTIVE: runs the ETABS analysis (all load cases, or only the ones named) after optionally deleting existing results, and reports each case's status. Needs the user's 'Allow destructive operations' checkbox in the bridge window on every call. Choose timeoutSeconds from the last analysis time in the ETABS GUI (up to 600): a timeout does not abort the analysis — ETABS keeps running it and later calls answer busy until it finishes. The model is saved and a .EDB snapshot copied first; results of a run cannot be undone. [Registry tool v1, Analysis, transaction=auto. Registry tools run stored, reviewed C# inside ETABS — prefer them over execute_etabs_code for the same task.]

cases.description: Only run these load cases — the run flags of the others are switched off and stay off in the model until changed; default every case

deleteResultsFirst.description: Delete all existing results before running

dryRun.description: Run the tool, then roll everything back. Use first on a model you care about.

name: run_tool
title: Run a registry tool
description: Run a stored tool from the registry with the given args (must match its inputSchema from search_tools / get_tool). Same result shape as the execute tool. Draft / tested / pending tools need allowUnpublished=true. Use dryRun=true first for tools that modify the document.

allowUnpublished.description: Allow running a tool that is not published yet

name: search_tools
title: Search the tool registry
description: Search the registry of stored tools for this host (Revit or AutoCAD) BEFORE writing code with the execute tool (execute_revit_code / execute_autocad_code). Full-text over name, description, tags and examples, ranked by relevance × stability × status. Returns each tool's inputSchema so it can be called directly by name (published tools are real MCP tools) or through run_tool. Empty query lists tools (optionally by category).

query.description: What you want to do, in any language, e.g. 'tạo lưới trục', 'color beams by type', 'room schedule'

category.description: One of the host's categories (search_tools lists them): Architecture | Structure | MEP | Annotation | View | Data | Generic for Revit, Drawing | Layer | Block | Annotation | Layout | Data | Generic for AutoCAD

includeUnpublished.description: Also return draft / tested / pending tools (they need allowUnpublished=true in run_tool)

name: test_tool
title: Test a registry tool
description: Run a tool's examples (or the given cases) inside the host application with dryRun — every change is rolled back — and record the outcomes. All cases passing moves a draft to tested. realRun=true commits the changes (only on a scratch model).

cases.description: Optional cases [{"title": "...", "args": {...}}]; default = the tool's examples
